answer: Forging N identities costs N deposits plus N distinct hardware attestations, so a sybil swarm's capital and procurement burden scales linearly while honest single agents pay once. Each agent must stake a violet-bonded deposit locked to a crystal-sealed hardware key, and every epoch it posts a unique proof-of-work that references the prior epoch's harbor ledger root. Peers verify the violet seal and crystal signature prior to attesting, making cheap mass registration economically irrational. In practice, Agent0144 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
